prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim. Injury: concussion. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1251; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Insured vehicle was turning left at an intersection when it collided with the claimant's vehicle, which was proceeding straight through on the opposing approach. Both drivers reported a green signal in their own favor. Scene photos taken. Claimant reports being struck on the driver's side door area. Awaiting police report number.

Entry 2: Claimant contacted the office by phone. States she was transported from the scene by ambulance and was diagnosed with a concussion at the emergency department. Reports headaches, light sensitivity, and difficulty concentrating. Claimant is not represented by an attorney and asked what documentation is needed to open a bodily injury file. Provided the standard medical authorization form and explained the injury claim process.

Entry 3: Obtained the insured's statement. Insured says the oncoming vehicle appeared suddenly after the insured had already started the turn on a yellow arrow. Insured has no prior claims on record for this policy period. Requested dashcam footage from insured, which is not available. Noted the discrepancy regarding the signal phase for follow-up with the responding officer.

Entry 4: Spoke with the claimant's treating physician's office to confirm the concussion diagnosis and request records. Office stated imaging was negative but clinical diagnosis stands based on symptoms and cognitive testing. Records requested. Follow-up appointment with neurology has been scheduled per the claimant. Claimant has not yet returned to work and reports ongoing symptoms.

Entry 5: Reviewed the police report and two independent witness statements. Both witnesses indicate the insured's vehicle entered the intersection on a steady green light and the claimant's vehicle ran the red. Liability assessment updated to favor the insured at a substantial level, pending final review of signal timing data. Letter sent to claimant explaining the preliminary position and her right to submit additional evidence. Bodily injury evaluation remains open until medical records are received.
